overview.title: Give people a product experience they can explore, not only watch.
paragraphs: We use Three.js to build purposeful browser-based 3D experiences, from product configurators and technical visualization to interactive campaign moments.
Every scene is planned around the content, device constraints, loading strategy, controls, and a useful fallback when WebGL is unavailable.

features.title: Interactive product scenes

features.title: Product configurators

banner.title: Have a product or idea that needs spatial interaction?
banner.description: Show us what people need to inspect, understand, configure, or experience in the browser.

faqs.question: When is Three.js the right choice?
faqs.answer: Three.js is useful when spatial interaction, product configuration, simulation, or visual explanation adds real value. We do not recommend it when a standard image or video communicates the same thing more clearly.

faqs.question: Can you work with existing 3D models?
faqs.answer: Yes. We review the model format, topology, materials, textures, and browser performance before confirming what optimization or rebuilding is needed.

faqs.question: Will the experience work on mobile devices?
faqs.answer: Mobile behavior is planned from the start. Scene detail, controls, camera framing, and loading strategy are adapted around practical device constraints.

faqs.question: Can Three.js work with our React or Vue application?
faqs.answer: Yes. The scene can be integrated as a focused rendering component while the surrounding product continues to use the existing application framework and state flow.

faqs.question: What happens when WebGL is unavailable?
faqs.answer: We provide an appropriate fallback, such as a still image, standard interface, or alternate product view, so essential information and actions remain available.
